title: Systems Addressing Frail Elders (SAFE) Care Implementation
brief_summary: Systems Addressing Frail Elders (SAFE) Care is a nurse-led interprofessional team model to rapidly identify and provide safe and effective inpatient care to high risk older adults and help support their successful transition back to the community. Developed and demonstrated to be effective in one hospital - the model is now being disseminated and studied in three additional hospitals (multiple organizational case study).
raw_criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

Organizational Leadership Nursing Unit Leadership/staff Adults aged 65 years

Exclusion criteria:

65 years and older that are on hospice protocols or dying/comfort care protocols.
study_population: This project does not have a set recruitment/enrollment goal. Process evaluation information will be collected by interview and observation of leadership and staff at three implementation sites. Quality Improvement (QI) outcome data will be collected involving elderly patients (\> 65 years) admitted to two med-surg units at each of the three collaborating sites over designated time periods: One month prior to implementation and six month after intervention. QI data from each hospital will be de-identified and submitted to core research team for analysis of patient outcomes.
